source.title: Progress on homogeneous Einstein manifolds and some open probrems

accepted.question_text: Let M = G/K be a homogeneous space, and call a G-invariant Riemannian metric Einstein when its Ricci tensor is a scalar multiple of the metric. Is Ziller's finiteness conjecture true: if the rank of G equals the rank of the isotropy subgroup, or if the isotropy representation of G/K decomposes into only non-equivalent irreducible summands, must the number of G-invariant Einstein metrics on M be finite?

evidence.quote: the number of G-invariant Einstein metrics is finite

accepted.question_text: For generalized flag manifolds G/K, where G is compact semisimple and K is the centralizer of a torus in G, can one develop methods that determine the total number and classification of G-invariant Einstein metrics for cases with many isotropy summands, especially generalized flag manifolds associated with classical Lie groups?
accepted.context_brief: Einstein metrics on generalized flag manifolds

evidence.quote: determining the total number of Einstein metrics

accepted.question_text: For Stiefel manifolds such as V_k R^n = SO(n)/SO(n-k), and more generally homogeneous spaces G/K whose isotropy representation contains equivalent summands, is the set of invariant Einstein metrics finite, or can continuous one-parameter families of invariant Einstein metrics occur?
accepted.context_brief: Equivalent isotropy summands and Stiefel manifolds

evidence.quote: one-parameter families of invariant Einstein metrics

needs_review.question_text_raw: Finally some open problems related to the generalized Wallach space SO(l + m + n)/(SO(l) x SO(m) x SO(n)) are listed in [ChNi].
